_comment: Capability catalog for the create-baw-portal BAW Bob skill. Task 1B.1 adds task retrieval, task detail, and task lifecycle operations. Do not prescribe UI frameworks, React components, or navigation patterns. Any feature-generation workflow must resolve before emitting code: hosting profile; NF vs PFS deployment; source-system routing; session-cookie vs applicable bearer-token authentication; cross-origin restrictions and proxy requirements; target BAW version; FDR/PFS prerequisites; and the existing application's technology stack. See references/hosting-and-generation.md; the detailed integration decision tree is deferred to the implementation playbook. STATUS SEMANTICS — status and evidence.level are independent dimensions: status describes contract completeness and deployment readiness; evidence.level describes the strength of supporting evidence. The deployment object is the authoritative source for NF/PFS/FDR/PFS-required restrictions regardless of status. (1) available: the advertised capability contract is implementable in a compatible environment; evidence may be runtime-verified or documentation-verified; required operations are either runtime-tested or have sufficient documentation evidence that deployment-time validation is expected to succeed. (2) partial: a material contract, coverage, or deployment-confidence gap remains — for example, a required operation has not been runtime-tested in any project environment, or an important prerequisite is not yet independently confirmed; additional deployment-time validation is required before relying on this capability in production. (3) gated: an explicit feature gate (e.g. FDR enabled) or deployment prerequisite (e.g. PFS registered) must be confirmed present before this capability can be used; the gate condition is stated in the prerequisites and deployment fields. (4) unverified: insufficient reliable supporting evidence exists; do not use without independent validation. Note: a capability may be 'available' while individual operations within it remain documentation-verified only — what matters is whether the overall contract can be fulfilled in a compatible environment.

enums._phase1DNote: These enum arrays are informational — they document valid values for human readers and the Task 1A lightweight inline validator. A future Task 1D validator must NOT derive its authoritative allowed-value lists by reading this catalog file at runtime; doing so would allow a bad actor to bypass validation simply by adding an unsupported value alongside a matching enum entry. The validator's authoritative enum lists must be defined inside the validator source (or a separate immutable schema file not modifiable through catalog edits) and must reject any catalog value not present in that hardcoded list.

conflicts.topic: Process-instance delete — HTTP DELETE endpoint vs PUT/POST action=delete
conflicts.description: IBM BAW 23.0.x REST API reference documents a dedicated DELETE /rest/bpm/wle/v1/process/{instanceId}?action=delete endpoint (topic=instance-delete-delete-process). In contrast, the IBM BAW/BPM REST API authorization reference (BAW 24.0.x and CP4BA 26.0.0) documents the delete operation exclusively as PUT /rest/bpm/wle/v1/process/{instanceId}?action={string} — no separate HTTP DELETE resource is described in those authorization tables. The authorization reference also notes that POST /rest/bpm/wle/v1/process/{instanceId}?action={string} is an equivalent alternate form. These two documentation sources cannot be reconciled from documentation alone: the DELETE method page may represent a convenience wrapper that internally dispatches action=delete, or it may be a version-specific variant. Implementations must verify which form (HTTP DELETE, PUT action=delete, or POST action=delete) is accepted in the specific target BAW deployment and version before relying on either in production code. Modeled operation NF-INSTANCE-DELETE uses the PUT form as the primary method, consistent with the authorization reference, and records this source conflict. Note: conflict entries do not support an externalProvenance field in the current schema; IBM documentation URLs are retained in docRefs here as an exception.

references/non-federated-api-guide.md, references/baw-rest.md, and validate-apis.mjs (NF16/NF17/NF20) use /searches/tasks/meta/*; earlier project notes used /searches/meta/* for NF, which returns 404 on BAW 24+. PFS uses /searches/meta/* everywhere. The NF runtime-verified path is /searches/tasks/meta/*.

references/non-federated-api-guide.md requires numeric id for PUT; references/baw-rest.md uses {idOrName} parameter and NF34 was tested by name. Workplace uses numeric id. Both may work; prefer numeric id for mutations.

The update path was not exercised; references/federated-api-guide.md confirms PFS05/PFS12–PFS19; references/baw-rest.md marks PUT as documentation-verified only (CREATE/READ/DELETE verified as PFS17). PUT update path not independently tested.

Two execution patterns are documented. (1) Direct GET: IBM documentation describes GET /tasks?savedSearch={idOrName} (NF) and GET /federated/v1/tasks?savedSearch={id} (PFS) as a single-step form that returns task results directly. Both are documentation-verified; neither has been runtime-tested in this project's environments. (2) Two-step pattern: GET the saved-search definition by id/name, then PUT /tasks (NF) or PUT /federated/v1/tasks (PFS) with criteria extracted from that definition — this is runtime-verified. These are alternative strategies: the operations belonging to each are not cumulative requirements. In the two-step pattern, stored fields must be replaced with an explicit alias list — fields:[] returns only TKIID/PIID/KIND. processName is not a valid alias (causes CWTBG0612E); use bpdName. Pagination: size and offset are valid URL query parameters for PUT /tasks (documentation-verified: IBM Search Execution Resource PUT for BAW 19.0.0 and 25.0.x, CP4BA 23.0.1/24.0.1/26.0.0); offset must never appear in the JSON body (causes CWTBG0618E). Runtime verification of query-param pagination is not available for this project's test environments.

POST /rest/bpm/wle/v2/search returns HTTP 503 when FDR is not enabled. NF35 (7 results on CP4BA 26.0.0) is a commit-message claim only; the retained run skipped it, so the endpoint is documentation-verified. Must gate on FDR detection before generating code for this endpoint. Project reference notes record that HTTP 503 with message ID CWTBG0788E indicates FDR is not enabled; this specific error-code-to-FDR-disabled mapping has not been independently tested on a known FDR-disabled environment in this project and was not independently confirmed in IBM documentation — treat it as a project-observed association, not a proven or confirmed-negative probe. See CAP-ADV-SEARCH-NF _strategyNote for the complete interpretation guide including inconclusive outcomes.

The previously documented data.search envelope was not observed and must not be silently accepted. Used as step 1 of the two-step execution strategy; in that strategy it is followed by NF-ADHOC-SEARCH with extracted criteria. operations.summary: Update a saved task search (NF)
operations.notes: Returns HTTP 200 with updated definition. PUT body must be complete: fetch full definition first, change only intended fields, include all others verbatim. With a complete 12-field body, all 11 non-modified fields were preserved in the subsequent GET (observed in a live rename-only test on CP4BA 26.0.3 SP20 r2, 2026-10-15). Whether a partial PUT body drops omitted fields (full-replacement) or retains them (merge) has not been independently demonstrated — do not assume either behavior. Numeric id addressing confirmed; name-based addressing not tested for mutations. NF34 was tested by name; Workplace uses numeric id. Prefer numeric id for mutations to avoid ambiguity.
limitations: Workplace convention uses numeric id, not name, for update — prefer numeric id for mutations

operations.summary: Delete a saved task search by ID or name (NF)
operations.notes: Returns HTTP 204 (No Content) with an empty response body on CP4BA 26.0.3 SP20 r2 — not 200. Accept 200 or 204 as success. operations.summary: Get personal task list (NF)
operations.notes: Use interaction=claimed_and_available for inbox-style view (all actionable tasks); use interaction=claimed to replicate Workplace's default. filterByCurrentUser and interaction are distinct parameters — do not treat as interchangeable. Response shape: data.items[] + data.totalCount + data.offset + data.size. data.stats may be null on some deployments — do not rely on it. totalCount is the server-reported total matching the query; items returned in one page are a bounded subset. Statistics computed from a single page describe that page only, not the full inbox. On some BAW deployments this endpoint returns a missing-default-search 404; only a 404 that passes the 404 classification in references/non-federated-api-guide.md and is confirmed by a usable NF-ADHOC-SEARCH (PUT /tasks) result switches to PUT.

operations.summary: Get federated task list (PFS)
operations.notes: Returns items[] from all federated source systems. Each item carries a systemID. Top-level federationResult[] (one entry per source system) provides taskCompletionUrlPrefix, restUrlPrefix, statusCode, and indexRefreshInterval for routing. Map task.systemID to the matching federationResult entry to obtain routing fields. Returns 404 on non-federated BAW. Partial failures possible — check federationResult[].statusCode for per-system HTTP 408/503. PFS01/PFS02 verified on CP4BA 26.0.0, two federated source systems. Live validation on a CP4BA 26.0.3 SP20 r2 development cluster (2026-10-16, single deployment): a task created by process start appeared with the expected state and the source systemID. PFS items carry no allowed-actions member — read actions from the source WLE. A task owned on a second registered system was absent from the federated list although it was directly retrievable from that system; that system reported taskSearchEnabled=false in PFS-SYSTEMS while the listed system reported true. That setting is a candidate explanation only (not proven; index/registration state not inspected). A ?systemID= query filter returned HTTP 500 on this deployment.
limitations: Returns 404 on non-federated BAW — requires PFS deployment
size=500 requests up to 500 tasks; surface truncation indicator when totalCount exceeds returned count
PFS index lag: results may not reflect the most recent task state on source systems — surface indexRefreshInterval from federationResult[]
Partial failures possible — a response may include results from only some source systems
A registered source system can be absent from items[] and federationResult[] (observed with taskSearchEnabled=false) — do not treat the federated list as every task the user owns
?systemID= as a query filter returned HTTP 500 on the CP4BA 26.0.3 SP20 r2 deployment — filter client-side on item systemID

operations.summary: Get task detail for a single task (NF)
operations.notes: Returns full task details including description, data, and available actions. runURL field is absent — task launch URL must be constructed manually via NF-TASK-LAUNCH. taskId must be a valid TKIID (numeric string on traditional BAW; UUID string on CP4BA). Do not validate TKIID with isNaN — UUID-format IDs fail that check. All returned values must be rendered via textContent, not unescaped innerHTML. NF06 verified on CP4BA 26.0.0. The action set differs by caller and task state (owner: cancel-claim, complete, reassign-to-user; non-owner: view only; administrator additionally: update priority, update due date, reassign-to-group). Treat actions as nullable and call parts=actions when action gating is needed.

operations.summary: Claim a task — assign to current user (NF)
operations.notes: Query: ?action=claim. Assigns the task to the currently authenticated user; task transitions to State_claimed. No request body required. NF23 verified on a pre-existing ready/available task; NF28 (newly started process task, lifecycle suite) is commit-message provenance only — the retained 2026-08-10 run skipped it; the runtime-verified label rests on NF23 alone. CSRF/XSRF requirement is verification-required per deployment, auth mode and API family; see references/non-federated-api-guide.md section XSRF / CSRF for WLE REST mutations.

NF-only: PFS-discovered tasks must be claimed via the owning source system's WLE endpoint (restUrlPrefix), not via PFS itself

operations.summary: Assign a task back to its original role (NF)
operations.notes: Query: ?action=assign&back=true. Assigns the claimed task back to the role or team it was originally routed to; task returns to State_ready and becomes available for another user to claim. Differs from action=cancel in that assign-back re-routes the task to its original assignment target, whereas action=cancel releases the current user's claim (see NF-TASK-CANCEL for cancel semantics). NF24 verified on CP4BA 26.0.0. Auth: session cookie (CSRF/XSRF requirement is verification-required; see references/non-federated-api-guide.md).
limitations: Task must be in State_claimed by the current user — assigning back a task the user does not own will fail
NF-only: route to source system for PFS-discovered tasks

operations.summary: Reassign a task to a user, group, or team (NF)
operations.notes: Query: ?action=assign combined with one of: toUser={username}, toGroup={groupName}, toTeam={teamName}, or toMe=true. Reassigns the task to the specified target. toUser, toGroup, toTeam, and toMe variants are documented in the BAW REST API reference. Only action=assign&back=true (NF24) was independently runtime-tested in this project — toUser/toGroup/toTeam/toMe are documentation-verified only. BAW enforces authorization at the task level; the API does not pre-validate the assignment target. Auth: session cookie (CSRF/XSRF requirement is verification-required; see references/non-federated-api-guide.md). Live validation on a CP4BA 26.0.3 SP20 r2 development cluster (2026-10-16, single deployment): only the toUser variant was exercised. Owner VTUser01 -> action=assign&toUser=<other user> returned HTTP 200; read-back showed owner changed to the target, whose action set then included cancel-claim, complete and reassign-to-user; the target then returned the task with toUser=<original user> (HTTP 200, owner read back). On a user-owned task no assign-back action was advertised for the owner; release used action=cancel. toGroup, toTeam and toMe were not tested and remain documentation-verified.
limitations: BAW enforces assignment authorization — unauthorized reassignment attempts will fail with an error
NF-only: route to source system for PFS-discovered tasks
Only toUser was verified on the live deployment; toGroup/toTeam/toMe remain documentation-verified

operations.summary: Complete (finish) a task (NF)
operations.notes: Query: ?action=finish. 'complete' is a server-side alias for 'finish' — use 'finish' as the canonical value. Task must be claimed by the current user. Output variable values are passed via the params query parameter as URL-encoded JSON; the required structure depends on the specific task definition. NF29 is defined in the lifecycle suite for a task with no required output variables but was skipped in the retained run. Auth: session cookie (CSRF/XSRF requirement is verification-required; see references/non-federated-api-guide.md). Provenance only (not verification): development commit messages fe28c62/bcadd98 claim NF29 passed on a CP4BA 26.0.0 runtime; no retained execution record exists (the retained 2026-08-10 run skipped NF26-NF36), so this operation is classified documentation-verified. Without the parts=all parameter, the response omits email, managerName, and jobTitle — always pass parts=all when those fields are needed. Response fields: data.fullName, data.displayName, data.userName, data.email (parts=all only), data.managerName (parts=all only), data.jobTitle (parts=all only). NF01 verified on CP4BA 26.0.0. Returns HTTP 401 when no active BAW session exists. BAW server-side scoping applies — the endpoint returns only the calling user's profile.
limitations: parts=all required to retrieve email, managerName, and jobTitle — default response omits these fields
data.managerName is a display name string, not a user ID — do not use it to discover managed-team membership or derive manager authorization; use NF-MANAGED-GLOBAL-TEAMS for that purpose
Returns only the calling user's own profile — cannot be used to retrieve another user's profile
Do not persist returned PII fields (email, managerName) in localStorage or other persistent client-side storage

operations.summary: Get global teams managed by the authenticated user (NF)
operations.notes: GET /rest/bpm/wle/v1/managedGlobalTeams. Returns the list of runtime global teams for which the authenticated user holds manager rights. Do not substitute profile attributes (managerName from NF-USER-CURRENT) or embedded user-response fields as a proxy for this endpoint. NF07 verified on CP4BA 26.0.0. Returns HTTP 200 with a list of managed global team objects; an empty list when the user manages no teams. BAW enforces the manager relationship server-side.

A returned managed-team list does not automatically grant task-mutation or instance-action permissions — BAW enforces those independently server-side
Team and group identifiers returned here must not be passed to the modeled-team endpoint NF-TEAM-BY-ID — global team IDs and modeled team IDs are not interchangeable
Do not derive manager authorization from embedded team data in the user-profile response — use this endpoint

operations.summary: Get all global teams visible to the authenticated user (NF)

capabilities.name: Advanced task searching (NF — FDR-gated)
capabilities.description: Execute advanced task queries using the WLE v2 search endpoint. Richer filter and sort capabilities than the v1 ad hoc search. Requires FDR to be enabled on the BAW instance; returns HTTP 503 otherwise. NF-only — no PFS equivalent. Must gate on FDR probe before using this capability. The required operation (NF-ADV-SEARCH) is runtime-verified; the optional query-management operation (NF-ADV-QUERIES-CREATE) is documentation-verified only.
capabilities._strategyNote: FDR detection strategy (no dedicated capability; deferred to the implementation playbook; no FDR status endpoint exists in the catalog). Candidate read-only probes: NF-ADV-QUERIES-LIST (GET /rest/bpm/wle/v2/search/queries; commit-message claim NF40 on an FDR-enabled environment, not retained; does not depend on team management) is the stronger positive probe (documentation-verified), and NF-DASHBOARD-TEAMSUMMARY-ALL (runtime-verified, NF10 retained HTTP 200) is a secondary probe that depends on the caller managing teams. Interpretation: HTTP 2xx from either — FDR-backed v2 endpoints are reachable. HTTP 503 whose body carries message ID CWTBG0788E — per project reference notes this indicates FDR is not enabled (this specific error-code-to-FDR-disabled mapping has not been independently tested on a known FDR-disabled environment in this project and was not independently confirmed in IBM documentation; treat as a project-observed association, not a proven-negative probe). Everything else is INCONCLUSIVE and must not be reported as FDR disabled: HTTP 400 (including CWTBG0805E when the caller manages no teams, or bad request), 401/403 (authentication or authorization), 404 (wrong prefix, version or topology), 408, other 5xx, CORS/proxy failure, network error or timeout. A BAW version number alone never proves FDR status. Cache the result per environment and re-probe on inconclusive outcomes; show a neutral empty state only for a confirmed negative.

evidence.environment: Documentation-verified (gated on FDR). NF35 and NF40 are commit-message provenance only; NF-ADV-QUERIES-CREATE is documentation-verified only.

capabilities.name: Core task lifecycle actions on PFS-discovered tasks (source-system routed)
capabilities.description: Composite for task actions initiated from a task discovered through Process Federation Server (PFS) and executed against the task's owning WLE/BPD source system. PFS exposes no task mutation endpoints. The core actions guaranteed by requiredOperations are: claim, assign-back, complete (finish), and cancel-claim — all executed against the source system via restUrlPrefix. Targeted reassignment to a specific user, group, or team (NF-TASK-ASSIGN-TO) and attribute update (NF-TASK-UPDATE) are optional extensions. PFS task discovery (PFS-TASK-LIST, PFS-ADHOC-SEARCH) is also optional — these operations are not required when validated routing context (systemID, restUrlPrefix, TKIID) is already known. The WLE v1 action operations are labelled non-federated because their metadata describes the target/source API contract, not the hosting topology; routing them via PFS discovery is intentional. The caller must resolve the owning source system from task.systemID via federationResult[], validate systemType == SYSTEM_TYPE_WLE, and validate restUrlPrefix against a trusted allowlist before sending any action request.
intents: claim, release, reassign, complete, or update a federated task

route task action to the owning source system
implement federated task inbox with actions
capabilities._strategyNote: Routing contract (all steps mandatory; fail closed on any failure). (1) Start from a task carrying systemID — from a PFS-TASK-LIST / PFS-ADHOC-SEARCH item or from validated existing context. (2) Resolve the single federationResult[] entry whose systemID equals task.systemID; zero or multiple matches is an error. (3) Require systemType == SYSTEM_TYPE_WLE before applying any WLE task-action contract; IBM documents SYSTEM_TYPE_WLE for process (BPD) systems, SYSTEM_TYPE_WPS for BPEL systems and SYSTEM_TYPE_CASE for Case systems — reject every other or missing value. (4) Take restUrlPrefix from that entry and validate it: normalized exact match against a trusted allowlist of configured source systems keyed by systemID; https scheme; no userinfo, query or fragment; no trailing slash; no dot-segments; path shape as documented by IBM (e.g. https://baw-host:9443/rest/bpm/wle) unless the allowlist explicitly records a different reverse-proxy path. Never use an unvalidated value from a response. (5) Build the action URL by appending only the relative path to the validated prefix: {restUrlPrefix}/v1/task/{encodeURIComponent(taskId)}?action=... . restUrlPrefix already ends in /rest/bpm/wle, so do NOT append /rest/bpm/wle again; do not blindly concatenate strings — construct with a URL parser and re-check the resulting origin equals the allowlisted origin. (6) Send the request directly to the source system (or to an allowlisted proxy that forwards to exactly that source system), never to the PFS REST host. (7) Source authentication, cross-origin and task authorization: a PFS session is not automatically valid for the source origin; confirm cross-system SSO or bearer-token coverage (CP4BA IAM bearer, or LTPA2/SAML spanning systems on standalone), configure the source-system CORS allowlist or a routing proxy (no open proxy / no caller-supplied target), and rely on the source system for task-level authorization — visibility in PFS does not imply permission to act. (8) PFS data is index-based and may be stale: an action can fail because the task already changed state. After any mutation, reconcile from the source system (NF-TASK-GET on the same validated prefix is authoritative), update the local row from that response, and re-query PFS only after the system's indexRefreshInterval; do not treat the next PFS list as immediately consistent. Feature-generation preflight (hosting profile, NF vs PFS, source-system routing, session-cookie vs bearer, CORS/proxy, target BAW version, FDR/PFS prerequisites, existing application stack) is defined in references/hosting-and-generation.md; the detailed integration decision tree is deferred to the implementation playbook.

capabilities._authNote: auth:pfs-session-cookie describes the credential used for PFS task-discovery requests (PFS-TASK-LIST, PFS-ADHOC-SEARCH) only. PFS discovery authentication and source-system mutation authentication are resolved independently. A valid PFS session does not guarantee authorization on the source system. Each source-system action request must be authenticated by a credential valid for that source origin — which may be source-specific cookies set during cross-system SSO, a bearer token with coverage over the source-system origin (e.g. CP4BA IAM bearer), LTPA2/SAML SSO spanning all source systems (standalone BAW), or an allowlisted server-side proxy that handles source-system authentication internally. The source API may reject requests that carry only PFS cookies. Credentials must never be sent to an unvalidated origin. Source routing must use a validated systemID and a restUrlPrefix from a trusted allowlist. SYSTEM_TYPE_WLE is required on the source system before applying the WLE v1 task-action contract.

capabilities.name: Process-instance lifecycle management (NF)
capabilities.description: Composite covering the complete documented set of BPD/WLE process-instance management actions on a non-federated BAW deployment: suspend, resume, retry, update due date, terminate, and delete. These are state-dependent alternatives, not a fixed sequential workflow: which action applies depends on the instance's current state and the caller's per-action authorization, and there is no mandatory order (terminate is not a prerequisite for delete). A known, authorized PIID is sufficient; instance listing or search is not required. A product that exposes only some of these actions must reference the individual action capabilities instead of claiming this composite.
intents: administer running, failed, or suspended process instances
capabilities._strategyNote: Alternatives, not a sequence: choose the action from the instance's current state (re-read it with NF-PROCESS-INSTANCE-GET when available) and treat server authorization as authoritative. Documented source states as recorded in this catalog: suspend — running/active; resume — Suspended; retry — Failed; update due date — active (running or suspended); terminate — Suspended, Failed, or Terminated per the authorization reference (do not assume any Active instance is terminable); delete — Suspended, Failed, or Terminated per the authorization reference (the BPM 8.5.0 REST reference also lists completed; verify in the target deployment). Authorization policies enforced server-side: ACTION_SUSPEND_INSTANCE, ACTION_RESUME_INSTANCE, ACTION_RETRY_INSTANCE, ACTION_CHANGE_INSTANCE_DUEDATE, ACTION_ABORT_INSTANCE, ACTION_DELETE_INSTANCE; a UI may hide actions but must not use that as the permission gate. Retry re-runs the failed service from its beginning and may repeat external side effects — require an idempotency assessment and confirmation, and never retry automatically or in loops. Terminate is irreversible and may affect child instances — require explicit confirmation showing process name and PIID. Delete is permanent and removes runtime history — require a separate explicit confirmation (distinct from any termination confirmation), write an application-level audit event (actor, PIID, process, timestamp, outcome; no process variable data) before submitting, and do not auto-retry a failed delete. Applies only to BPD/WLE instances, not BPEL/BFM. Deployment-specific checks before exposing an action: BAW version, accepted HTTP method for delete (conflict C06), accepted dueDate format, and whether the caller's role holds each policy. A caller who already holds a valid authorized PIID needs no listing call. Instance actions on PFS-discovered instances (PFS-INSTANCES-SEARCH) are not modeled here; they would require source-system routing as in CAP-TASK-LIFECYCLE-PFS. Feature-generation preflight (hosting profile, NF vs PFS, authentication, CORS/proxy, target BAW version, existing application stack) is defined in references/hosting-and-generation.md; the detailed decision tree is deferred to the implementation playbook.
